seoTitle: Pemba Island Tanzania — Diving, Nature & Off-the-Beaten-Path Guide 2026
intro: Pemba Island is the lesser-known island of the Zanzibar Archipelago — smaller, greener, and more rugged than Zanzibar, with no mass tourism and some of the best wall diving in the western Indian Ocean. Located 80 kilometres north of Zanzibar Island, Pemba's steep underwater walls drop hundreds of metres into the Pemba Channel, creating currents that feed exceptional coral growth and pelagic fish populations.

sections.heading: World-Class Wall Diving
sections.content: Pemba's dive sites are among the Indian Ocean's finest, largely unknown outside serious diving circles. The Pemba Channel drops to 800 metres within a few kilometres of shore. The underwater walls are covered in pristine soft corals, sea fans, and sponges. Hammerhead sharks, manta rays, whale sharks (October–February), barracuda, and tuna frequent the channel. Visibility typically exceeds 30 metres. The island has a fraction of Zanzibar's dive traffic, meaning sites remain in exceptional condition. Several dive operators run day trips and liveaboard charters specifically for Pemba diving.

sections.heading: The Island Landscape
sections.content: Pemba is genuinely different from Zanzibar Island — steep, forested hills, clove plantations covering the interior, mangrove channels winding through the coastline, and a persistent breeze that keeps temperatures comfortable. The island is still predominantly agricultural — cloves, coconuts, and seaweed farming are the main industries. Village life is largely undisturbed by tourism. The island's Swahili culture has distinct characteristics from Zanzibar, including unique musical traditions and traditional healing practices associated with Pemba's historically powerful spirit mediums.

sections.heading: Getting to Pemba Island
sections.content: Pemba is accessible by two options. By air: Coastal Aviation and Auric Air run scheduled flights from Zanzibar (30 minutes) and Dar es Salaam (1 hour). By ferry: a high-speed ferry connects Zanzibar to Pemba Chake Chake port (2.5–3 hours) twice weekly — check current schedules as services change seasonally. Accommodation is limited to small guesthouses and a handful of eco-lodges — Pemba Lodge and Manta Resort are the standout options with direct beach and dive access.

faqs.q: Is Pemba Island good for snorkelling?
faqs.a: Yes but diving is the primary draw. The wall diving begins relatively shallow (8–15 metres) so snorkellers can see the top of the coral formations, but the most dramatic marine life is at depth. Some shallow reef areas near the coast are accessible for snorkelling.

faqs.q: How do I get from Zanzibar to Pemba Island?
faqs.a: By air: 30 minutes on Coastal Aviation or Auric Air. By ferry: 2.5–3 hours on the high-speed ferry from Zanzibar, running twice weekly. Most visitors fly to minimise travel time given Pemba's limited accommodation supply.

faqs.q: How many days should I spend on Pemba Island?
faqs.a: 3–5 days is ideal for serious divers. Casual visitors combining it with Zanzibar typically do 2 days. Pemba is not suitable for visitors looking for beach resort infrastructure — accommodation is limited and the island rewards active, exploratory travellers.

tips: Book dive operators and accommodation at least 2 months ahead — capacity is very limited
Fly rather than take the ferry — save time for more dives
The best diving is October–March for whale sharks and clearest visibility
Hire a local guide for the clove farm interior — the landscape is extraordinary
Combine with Zanzibar Island for a full Zanzibar Archipelago experience
